This guide covers 20 live sports options in Chattanooga. The listings span teams, spectator events, and sports bars across the city and nearby neighborhoods.
Erlanger Park opened in April 2026, bringing the Chattanooga Lookouts to the South Broad District. The new 8,000-seat ballpark uses the historic Power House building as its main entrance. It sits on the old U.S. Pipe foundry site on the South Broad waterfront.
Four professional teams play home games here: Chattanooga FC and the UTC Mocs share Finley Stadium for soccer and football, the Lookouts play at Erlanger Park, and the Chattanooga Strike play ABA basketball at Midtown Arena. The Red Wolves soccer club plays at CHI Memorial Stadium in East Ridge.
The Free filter narrows to three options where watching costs nothing: Covenant College regular season basketball on top of Lookout Mountain, the IRONMAN triathlon at Ross’s Landing each September, and the Head of the Hooch rowing regatta each November. The East Ridge filter clusters four options in one area, including CHI Memorial Stadium and Camp Jordan Arena.

Professional Sports in Chattanooga.

Chattanooga has four active professional teams. Chattanooga FC plays MLS Next Pro soccer at Finley Stadium with one of the most loyal fan bases in the city. The Red Wolves bring a second pro soccer option in East Ridge. The Lookouts have been the city’s baseball anchor since 1885, now at the new Erlanger Park on the South Broad waterfront. The Strike play ABA basketball at Midtown Arena with a rules format that inflates scores in the final minutes.

Live music at Finley StadiumRestaurants near Erlanger Park

Sports Bars in Chattanooga.

Downtown Chattanooga has Parkway Pourhouse on Riverfront Parkway and Southside Social on Chestnut Street. The Southside has Shady’s Corner for a dive-bar crowd. North Shore keeps Tremont Tavern on Hixson Pike. Camp Jordan in East Ridge clusters Jonathan’s Grille and Twin Peaks within walking distance, near CHI Memorial Stadium. Miller’s Ale House on Gunbarrel Road runs more than 60 TVs for the NFL Sunday crowd.

Chattanooga breweries guide

Downtown Chattanooga Sports.

Finley Stadium and McKenzie Arena are both in the downtown core. UTC football and Chattanooga FC both play at Finley. Both UTC basketball teams play at McKenzie Arena on McCallie Ave. Erlanger Park is a short drive south in the South Broad District. IRONMAN and Head of the Hooch fill Ross’s Landing on the riverfront each fall. Parkway Pourhouse and Southside Social cover game-day bar options nearby.

Restaurants with a view near the waterfront

East Ridge Sports.

East Ridge is about 10 minutes from downtown and clusters several options in the Camp Jordan area. CHI Memorial Stadium hosts Red Wolves SC home games. Camp Jordan Arena is the home of Chattanooga Roller Derby. Jonathan’s Grille and Twin Peaks are within walking distance of each other on the same strip, easy to combine before or after a Red Wolves match.

1. UTC Mocs Football .

FCS Division 1 program in the Southern Conference, playing since 1904. Home games at Finley Stadium in downtown Chattanooga, a 20,000-seat AstroTurf facility. Season runs late August through late November. Terrell Owens, former NFL Hall of Famer, played here from 1992 to 1995. A street in town, Terrell Owens Way, bears his name. The east side student section has the most energy. The shaded west side near the press box is a quieter option.

2. High School Football .

Friday night high school football around Chattanooga features several competitive programs. Notable schools include the Baylor Red Raiders, McCallie Blue Tornado, East Hamilton Hurricanes, and Signal Mountain Eagles. Baylor and McCallie met in the 2024 state championship. Finley Stadium hosts key rivalry and playoff games, giving young athletes a professional field. Check individual school athletic sites for schedules.

3. Chattanooga FC .

Professional soccer club founded in 2009, now playing in MLS Next Pro. Home games at Finley Stadium, which holds about 20,000 fans. The devoted local fan base is known as the Chattahooligans. Season runs March through October. In 2019 the club became one of the first American sports teams to offer fan ownership shares. Family events run throughout the season.
Google Maps Tickets Schedule

4. Chattanooga Red Wolves SC .

USL League One club founded in 2018 at CHI Memorial Stadium in East Ridge, Tennessee's first soccer-specific venue. The stadium holds about 5,500 fans. Season runs March through October. The club also fields a women's team in the USL W League at the same venue. Family-friendly events run throughout the year including Rusty's Birthday Bash and an Easter Egg hunt.

5. UTC Mocs Men's Basketball .

Division 1 SoCon program playing since 1977 with 12 NCAA tournament appearances. Best run was a 1997 Sweet Sixteen as a 14-seed, defeating Georgia and Illinois before losing to Providence. Twelve SoCon tournament titles, most recently in 2022. Home games at McKenzie Arena, season November through February. McKenzie Arena enforces a clear bag policy at the door.

6. UTC Lady Mocs Basketball .

Division 1 SoCon program competing since 1977. Twenty SoCon conference championships, the most in conference history. Seventeen NCAA tournament appearances, most recently advancing to the Final 32 in 2004. Most recent conference title came in 2024 over UNC Greensboro. Home games at McKenzie Arena, season November through February. McKenzie Arena enforces a clear bag policy at the door.

7. Chattanooga Strike .

American Basketball Association (ABA) team that joined the league in 2024. Home games at Midtown Arena on a 20-game schedule running late October through February. The ABA uses a 7-second half-court rule that lights a 3D scoring light. When the light is on, two-point shots count as three, three-pointers count as four, and half-court shots count as five points.

8. Covenant College Scots Basketball .

Division III program atop Lookout Mountain at Barnes Physical Education Center. Regular season home games are free. Men's and women's teams compete in the Collegiate Conference of the South, season November through February. High-level basketball, on top of a mountain, at no cost. Take a walk around campus after the game.

9. Chattanooga Lookouts .

AA minor league baseball team with a history stretching back to 1885. Moved to Erlanger Park in the South Broad District in April 2026 after leaving AT&T Field. The new ballpark seats about 8,000 and uses the historic Power House building as its main entrance. In 1931, 17-year-old Chattanoogan Jackie Mitchell struck out Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig in an exhibition game against the Yankees. Hall of Famers including Nolan Ryan, Satchel Paige, and Willie Stargell all had stints with the club. Game promos include $0.25 hot dog nights and fireworks Fridays.

10. IRONMAN Chattanooga .

Annual full IRONMAN triathlon each September. Athletes swim the Tennessee River, bike through North Georgia, then run a marathon back through downtown Chattanooga. Free to watch from the riverbank at Ross's Landing. A shorter IRONMAN 70.3 runs in the spring on the same course. Both events bring thousands of athletes to the downtown riverfront.

11. Head of the Hooch Regatta .

Annual November rowing regatta at Ross's Landing and one of the largest in the country. More than 6,000 rowers compete each year. Boats race downstream and free viewing spots line the riverbank. Easy afternoon or full-day spectator event at the downtown waterfront. No ticket required.

12. Chattanooga Roller Derby .

Flat-track roller derby with home bouts at Camp Jordan Arena in East Ridge. The Ruby Regulators and B-Railers are the two home teams. Regular season runs spring through summer with home bouts typically April through June. The annual Nooga Knockdown tournament brings clubs from across the region to Camp Jordan in late July.

13. Nooga Rugby .

Men's and women's rugby clubs based at 1151 East 23rd Street in Chattanooga. The men's program was founded in 1978 and has seven conference championship titles in the True South conference. The women's team, the Chattanooga Queens, competes in Division II and III leagues. Season runs January through April. Home matches are open to spectators.

14. Parkway Pourhouse .

Cajun and Creole-inspired sports bar on Riverfront Parkway in downtown Chattanooga. Serves gumbo, crawfish étouffée, po'boys, and wings alongside local beers and cocktails. Multiple TV screens inside and on a large covered outdoor patio. Dog-friendly patio works well for outdoor game watching on fall evenings.

15. Southside Social .

Bowling and sports bar at 1818 Chestnut St with 10 boutique bowling lanes, four bars, and a full kitchen. Games include cornhole, ping pong, billiards, and arcade. Multiple screens for game days. Family-friendly setup works for groups with kids as well as adult crowds. Open Tuesday through Sunday.

16. Tremont Tavern .

FAQ.

Where do the Chattanooga Lookouts play in 2026?

Erlanger Park in the South Broad District, which opened April 14, 2026. The 8,000-seat ballpark sits on the old U.S. Pipe foundry site. The historic Power House building forms the main entrance. It replaced AT&T Field as the team’s home after the 2025 season.

What professional sports teams are based in Chattanooga?

Four professional teams: Chattanooga Lookouts (AA minor league baseball), Chattanooga FC (MLS Next Pro soccer), Chattanooga Red Wolves SC (USL League One soccer), and the Chattanooga Strike (ABA basketball). All four play home games within or near Chattanooga.

Are there free sports events to watch in Chattanooga?

Yes. Covenant College basketball at Barnes PE Center on Lookout Mountain is free for regular season home games. IRONMAN Chattanooga in September is free to watch from the riverbank at Ross’s Landing. The Head of the Hooch rowing regatta each November is also free from the riverfront.

What are the best sports bars in Chattanooga for watching NFL games?

Miller’s Ale House on Gunbarrel Road runs more than 60 TVs and draws large Sunday crowds. Parkway Pourhouse downtown has indoor and outdoor screens including a covered patio. Camp Jordan in East Ridge has Jonathan’s Grille and Twin Peaks within walking distance of each other.

Who is Jackie Mitchell and what did she do?

Jackie Mitchell was a 17-year-old pitcher from Chattanooga who struck out Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig in a 1931 exhibition game between the New York Yankees and the Chattanooga Lookouts. She is widely regarded as one of the first women to sign a professional baseball contract.

What sports teams play at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga?

Finley Stadium hosts UTC Mocs FCS football (season late August through November), Chattanooga FC soccer (season March through October), and key high school football games throughout the fall. The stadium holds about 20,000 fans and sits in downtown Chattanooga. It also hosts occasional live music events.
